newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - Stock market views on UK election.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Stock market views on UK election.

text.p: The following is a selection of reactions from stock market strategists to confirmation that British Prime Minister has called an election on May 1.

"This can hardly come as a surprise, it was the date everyone was pencilling in and I don't think it will change perceptions towards the UK equity market. Markets are supposed to be rational discounters and there had been plenty of time to digest this.
"The (UK stock) market looks good value relative to European and other global markets and once the election is out of the way I think we will be able to focus back on the fundamentals.
"With the economy slowing down next year and an increased chance of sterling going into a single European currency, gilts look relatively good value and that should be good for equities."
"Back in March 1992 the market fell 1.9 percent on the election announcement, when Labour were about three percent ahead in the polls.
"This time around they are about 26 percent ahead in the polls and the level of discounting is much, much greater, and this should be played out in stock movements.
"I expect a bit of a knee-jerk reaction or wobbling, but nothing like the same scale as in 1992."

"As far as the equity market is concerned I think we will probably just drift along... the factors driving us such as U.S. interest rate prospects will still have a major influence but I would be surprised if there is much progress on the upside before May 1.

"I would be reluctant to say what the UK market has discounted, there is clearly an expectation that the outcome will be a Labour majority but if there is a worse scenario it could be that the polls get close near the election.
"If Labour does what it says it will do it should not make much difference to the market's prospects...the thing is we don't know any of the detail of what they will do.
"Clearly there is a bit of downside risk given the performance we have already seen this year but it is quite plausible we we see a recovery once the uncertainty is out of the way."
